ledger.claim: The driver never placed the in-app call that POL-NS-23 requires. The record's own contact check reports contact_before_cancel.call_count = 0 with an empty calls array (EV-TRIP-06056), and the single in-app call on this trip was placed by the RIDER at 16:06:10 and went unanswered — in_app_calls shows placed_by 'RIDER', answered false (EV-TRIP-06056). POL-NS-23 requires at least one in-app call from the driver before trip_record.cancelled_at (16:09:30). That limb fails, so the fee is voided: the rider is not charged and there is no driver compensation.

Independently, the driver sent the rider no in-app chat message before cancelling. The chat log is complete and weighs 1.0 (EV-CHAT-06056): it holds exactly two messages, MSG-06056-001 and MSG-06056-002, and the sender on both is 'RIDER' — the driver's share of the conversation is zero, matching contact_before_cancel.message_count = 0 (EV-TRIP-06056). Under POL-NS-23 the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call; each limb is independently sufficient, and the message limb fails here as well.

Because POL-NS-23 is breached, the measure is a full refund of the 5.00 SGD actually charged, not a partial one. The payments ledger is complete at weight 1.0 and shows total_charged = 5.00 SGD against the cancellation fee, payment_status 'CHARGED', and refund_issued_sgd = 0.0 (EV-FARE-06056); there is nothing left on the rider's side of the ledger to set against it, so refund_if_voided_sgd = 5.00 (EV-FARE-06056) is the whole of what the rider is owed. I accept that the cancellation came at 16:09:30, after the free wait that expired at 16:03:15 — but POL-NS-23 voids the fee where contact was not attempted regardless of that timing, and it is POL-NS-23, not POL-NS-22's compensation rule, that governs a fee taken without the required contact.

The driver's account that he was 'at the pickup point waiting' is contradicted by his own device trace. The arrival check on the complete, 1.0-weight GPS trace reports corroborated = false and a nearest fix of 364.96 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 9.0 m (EV-GPS-06056) — far outside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that the category sets for this zone class. The trace also shows the vehicle stationary (speed_kph 0) at that same spot from 15:58:00 through the 16:09:30 cancellation (EV-GPS-06056). The record's arrival event at 15:58:10 is therefore not a marking made at the pickup location, and the rider's own account — that the driver was never at Blk 520 — is the account the evidence supports.

On the corroborated facts the driver is the party who failed to reach the pickup point, which is the POL-NS-24 case: the driver did not arrive at the pickup location by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes, so the rider may not be charged and any fee charged is refunded in full. The scheduled time was 16:00 and the deadline 16:05:00 (EV-TRIP-06056), and the driver's trace never brings him within the 50 m arrival radius of the pickup point at any time before the cancellation (EV-GPS-06056). The 5.00 SGD taken at 16:09:34 must therefore be returned to the rider in full (EV-FARE-06056).

The second limb of POL-NS-24 is also made out: the driver, having failed to reach the pickup point, also failed to attempt contact at all — no chat message (EV-CHAT-06056) and no in-app call (EV-TRIP-06056) from the driver at any point before he cancelled. The rider is accordingly due the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit (EV-FARE-06056, goodwill_credit_sgd = 5.00). I raise this as the referral POL-GEN-03 describes, naming POL-NS-24 in the ruling object; the referral sits alongside the refund and does not displace it.

The rider's own conduct on this trip was that of a waiting passenger: he messaged the driver in-app at 16:02:00 ('I'm at the Blk 520 drop off, I don't see you') and again at 16:05:30, both read by the driver at 16:02:27 and 16:05:51 respectively, and he placed an in-app call at 16:06:10 that rang 25 seconds unanswered (EV-CHAT-06056, EV-TRIP-06056). The trace carries no rider track, so rider_presence is unavailable (EV-GPS-06056) and the rider's presence cannot be corroborated by positioning — but his waiting and his attempts to reach the driver are established by the chat log and the call record, both complete at weight 1.0, and nothing in the record shows the rider leaving.

The traffic advisory for this trip is absent: EV-ADVIS-06056-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, has admissibility weight 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I rely on it only as that absence. It carries no fact for either side, and in particular it cannot supply the driver with a traffic excuse for holding 364.96 m short of the pickup point for the whole wait (EV-GPS-06056); no other traffic evidence is on the record either.

This case does not need a human because a fact is missing. POL-GEN-26 escalates where a needed fact cannot be established, but the facts POL-NS-23 turns on — whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling — are carried by artifacts that are COMPLETE with no issues and weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-06056, EV-CHAT-06056), and the timing facts come from the same complete trip record. The contact question is settled on the record, so it is answered, not escalated.

No repeat no-show referral arises against this rider. The rider's profile carries no_show_cancellations_30d = 0 (EV-RPROF-06056), and POL-NS-25 requires a count of 3 or more, counting this trip, before any flag is recorded. In any event the fee should not stand here, so the count cannot move.

The trip record puts the driver's arrival event at 15:58:10, before the 16:00:00 scheduled pickup, so POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from the scheduled time and it expired at 16:05:00; the driver cancelled at 16:09:30 and the record's derived free-wait figures return cancelled_after_free_wait true with 570 s from the wait's start to the cancellation, so the cancellation came after the free wait and the timing precondition for a rider-no-show cancellation is met.

POL-NS-22 fixes the no-show cancellation fee at 5.00 SGD, charged to the rider and transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel; the payments ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 16:09:34 and the record's derived money block returns fee_matches_policy true, so the amount charged is exactly the policy amount and no fee-amount defect arises.

On a no-show where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the fee charged, 5.00 SGD; the driver cancelled only after the free wait and the amount charged is the policy amount, so that is the ruling this record supports, and the driver should not carry the time and fuel of an unattended scheduled pickup.

The record's derived driver-deadline check returns arrived_by_deadline true against the 16:05:00 deadline, so on the trip record the driver did not fail to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus five minutes; the rider's no-charge cancellation right under POL-NS-24 is keyed to exactly that failure and so never arose, and POL-NS-24 returns no part of this fee.

The rider had notice and did not board: the platform pushed 'Your driver has arrived' at 15:58:14, the wait timer expired at 16:03:15 with the rider not on board, and the rider's own messages at 16:02 and 16:05 show the rider on the app and engaged during the wait; the rider's non-appearance is what caused this cancellation, so the 5.00 SGD charged is a genuine no-show fee under POL-NS-22 rather than an error.

The driver's device trace is complete and gap-free (50 fixes, coverage 100%, max gap 30 s) and its fixes from 15:58:00 to the 16:09:30 cancellation all report speed 0 at a single position, an unbroken stop of roughly eleven and a half minutes; that dwell is consistent with the driver's statement that he waited more than ten minutes for the rider and did not abandon the job.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged on trip TRP-06056 cannot stand, and the rider is refunded it in full.

Why the fee is voided. POL-NS-23 requires that, before cancelling for a no-show, the driver must have both sent the rider an in-app chat message and placed an in-app call, both before the cancellation at 16:09:30. He did neither. The trip record's own contact check (EV-TRIP-06056) returns a call count of 0 and a message count of 0, and the complete chat log (EV-CHAT-06056, weight 1.0) holds only the rider's two messages — the single in-app call on this trip was placed by the rider at 16:06:10 and went unanswered. With either limb missing, POL-NS-23 voids the fee: the 5.00 SGD charged (EV-FARE-06056, cancellation_fee 5.00 SGD, charged 16:09:34, refund_issued_sgd 0.0) is returned in full, and no compensation flows to the driver.

The failed arrival. The category's arrival test requires the trip record's 'arrived' marker to be corroborated by the GPS trace within the 50 m STANDARD radius. It is not: the driver's complete device trace (EV-GPS-06056, weight 1.0, 50 fixes, coverage 100%, no gaps) puts the nearest fix about 365 m from Block 520, Serangoon North Avenue 4, and shows the vehicle stationary there from 15:58:00 until the four minutes past the deadline cancellation. The driver's statement that he was 'at the pickup point waiting more than 10 minutes' is outweighed by his own trace, and POL-NS-24 is independently satisfied: the driver never reached the pickup by the 16:05:00 deadline (scheduled 16:00 plus five minutes).

Driver's points. The arguments that the free-wait timing precondition was met (POL-NS-21: the driver marked arrival at 15:58:10 before the 16:00 schedule, so the 300 s wait ran to 16:05:00 and the cancellation at 16:09:30 came after it) and that the fee is exactly the policy 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22, fee_matches_policy true) are correct as far as they go, but they do not save the fee: the contact obligation in POL-NS-23 is a separate requirement and it was breached. For the same reason the DRIVER_COMPENSATION claim under POL-NS-22 is rejected — the fee does not stand, so its transfer to the driver does not arise. The claim that the driver 'arrived by the deadline' (POL-NS-24) rests only on the trip record's uncorroborated marker and is rejected. The points that the rider was on the app and did not board, and that the trace shows a stationary dwell, are accepted, but they show the rider waiting and the driver stopped roughly 365 m short of the pickup; they do not revive the fee.

Rider's other points are accepted. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06056-01) is MISSING, weight 0.0, and carries no fact for either side; and the facts this case turns on are carried by complete, weight-1.0 artifacts, so no escalation arises under POL-GEN-26.

Goodwill credit. Because the driver both failed to arrive and failed to attempt contact, POL-NS-24 also gives the rider a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit (EV-FARE-06056, goodwill_credit_sgd 5.00), recorded as the referral below; it sits alongside the refund and does not change it. No repeat no-show flag arises under POL-NS-25 (the rider's no_show_cancellations_30d is 0).

Confidence 0.95. The deciding facts — the missing contact and the failed arrival — are carried by artifacts weighted 1.0 (EV-TRIP-06056, EV-CHAT-06056, EV-GPS-06056), so the cap is 1.0. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final and no fraud flag applies.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-24: record the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit to the rider, the driver having both failed to reach the pickup point and failed to attempt contact (EV-FARE-06056, goodwill_credit_sgd = 5.00).
